analysis.investment_thesis: Nesco is a fortress-balance-sheet owner of irreplaceable Mumbai exhibition and IT-park real estate, generating 50%+ operating margins and a clean 12% revenue CAGR over nine years — exactly the steady compounder I respect. However, a massive capex cycle (CWIP surged to ₹761 Cr, FCF turned -₹435 Cr in FY25) and a P/E touching 20.8x stretch the margin of safety at current prices.
key_strengths: Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.04) even mid-capex cycle — fortress balance sheet that passes my strictest test
Irreplaceable Mumbai land (BEC Goregaon) creates a genuine geographic moat with 50.9% operating margins
Promoter holding at 68.5% is stable and high — skin in the game, aligned with minority shareholders
key_risks: Massive CWIP of ₹761 Cr (up from ₹162 Cr in FY24) signals aggressive expansion — execution risk on new capacity is real
Exhibition/events revenue is cyclically vulnerable — FY21 showed a sharp 33% revenue drop during COVID, a reminder this is not truly defensive
Other income (₹114 Cr in FY25) constitutes ~30% of net profit — inflated by investment income, masking operating earnings quality
red_flags: FCF turned deeply negative at -₹435 Cr in FY25 — the largest capex outlay in company history (₹784 Cr) needs to prove returns
ROE at 15.8% is below my 18-22% target range, and will likely dilute further as massive new assets come online before generating revenue
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Nesco ticks most of my checklist on quality: the Bombay Exhibition Centre and IT park in Goregaon represent genuinely irreplaceable Mumbai real estate — you cannot replicate this land in this city. Operating margins at 50.9% are extraordinary and reflect real pricing power. The nine-year revenue CAGR of 12% and net profit CAGR of 11.2% are precisely the kind of steady, boring compounding I love. Balance sheet discipline is exceptional — near-zero debt for most of the past decade, with reserves compounding from ₹1,343 Cr in FY20 to ₹2,785 Cr in FY25.

My hesitation is the FY25 capex surge. CWIP jumped to ₹761 Cr and free cash flow cratered to -₹435 Cr — this is the largest capital deployment in the company's history. The business is funding this through internal accruals and modest borrowings (₹110 Cr), so the balance sheet stays intact, but returns on this new capacity are unproven. At P/E 20.8x — the very top of my comfort range — there is little margin of safety if the expansion takes longer than expected to fill up. I would watch for capacity utilisation metrics on the new halls and ROCE stability before adding meaningfully. Worth owning a small position, but not loading up at current prices.
